## Introduction

This vignette reproduces the simulation example of the README.  It evaluates
transfer-learning methods for survival prediction under covariate shift.
The workflow:

1.  generate simulated target, deployment and external datasets,
2.  screen the external datasets for transferability,
3.  estimate density-ratio weights for covariate-shift correction,
4.  fit multiple Cox-based models,
5.  evaluate predictive performance using Harrell's C-index,
    time-dependent AUC and the Brier score.

![workflow](workflow.png){width=80%}

```{r setup}
library(CoxRTL)
library(survival)
library(survcomp)
library(timeROC)
library(survAUC)
set.seed(123)
```

## 1. Set simulation parameters

```{r params}
# Sample sizes
N <- 50000      # Total size of the covariate pool used for sampling
Ns <- 500       # Sample size for each external dataset
Nt <- 200       # Sample size for the target dataset
nt_all <- 1000  # Total sample size of the deployment dataset
nt <- 500       # Size of the calibration subset drawn from the deployment dataset

# Number of covariates
p <- 100

# Survival parameters
kappa_t <- 4    # Baseline hazard parameter for the target/deployment data
kappa_s <- 2    # Baseline hazard parameter for the external data

# Penalized Cox regression parameters
lambda <- "lambda.min"   # Alternative choice: "lambda.1se"
alpha <- 0.5               # Ridge penalty; alternative choices: 1 (lasso) or 0.5 (elastic net)

# Covariate shift parameters
ratio_scale_TeS <- 0.5   # Shift magnitude between deployment and external datasets
ratio_scale_TeTr <- 0.5  # Shift magnitude between deployment and target dataset
```

## 2. Generate simulated datasets

```{r generate, results = "hide"}
sim <- gen_surv_data(
  N = N,
  Ns = Ns,
  Nt = Nt,
  nt = nt_all,
  kappa_t = kappa_t,
  kappa_s = kappa_s,
  ratio_scale_TeS = ratio_scale_TeS,
  ratio_scale_TeTr = ratio_scale_TeTr,
  p = p,
  num_Xs = 3
)
```

`gen_surv_data()` returns a list with three components: `data_s` (a list
of external datasets), `data_train` (the target dataset) and `data_test` (the
deployment dataset).

Split the deployment dataset into a calibration subset, used to estimate the
density-ratio weights, and an evaluation subset, used for model assessment:

```{r split}
sample_calibrate <- sample(1:nt_all, nt)

data_calibrate <- sim$data_test[sample_calibrate, ]
data_evaldata  <- sim$data_test[-sample_calibrate, ]

# Target and external datasets
data_target <- sim$data_train
data_s <- sim$data_s

# Sizes of the four pieces of data
c(target = nrow(data_target),
  calibration = nrow(data_calibrate),
  evaluation = nrow(data_evaldata),
  external = sum(vapply(data_s, nrow, integer(1))))
```

## 3. Prepare model inputs

```{r inputs}
# Combine all external datasets
X_s_all <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(i) {
  as.matrix(data_s[[i]][, 1:p])
}))

time_s_all <- do.call(c, lapply(1:3, function(i) data_s[[i]]$time))
status_s_all <- do.call(c, lapply(1:3, function(i) data_s[[i]]$status))
y_s_all <- Surv(time = time_s_all, event = status_s_all)

# Target dataset
X_target <- as.matrix(data_target[, 1:p])
y_target <- Surv(data_target$time, data_target$status)

# Deployment subsets
X_calibrate <- as.matrix(data_calibrate[, 1:p])
X_evaldata  <- as.matrix(data_evaldata[, 1:p])

# Predictor names
covariates <- colnames(data_target)[1:p]
```

## 4. Screen the external datasets for transferability

Borrowing information from an external dataset only helps when its
predictor-outcome relationship is close enough to the target domain.
`detect_transferable()` screens each candidate external dataset by its
predictive gain in the target domain before anything is weighted or pooled. It
partitions the target dataset into `V` folds and, within each fold, compares two
penalized Cox models, both using the same `alpha` as the model fits below and
both evaluated on the held-out target fold with Harrell's C-index:

-   a **target-only** model fitted on the target fitting folds, and
-   a **two-step transfer** model that pools the candidate external dataset with
    the target fitting folds and then applies a target-based debiasing
    correction.

The average difference across folds is `delta_C` and its median is
`delta_C_median`. Under the `rule = "median"` used below a dataset is declared
transferable when `delta_C_median` exceeds `threshold` (0 by default), and the
verdict is reported in the `transferable` column of the summary table, next to
the gains it was derived from.

```{r screen, warning = FALSE}
X_s_list <- lapply(data_s, function(d) as.matrix(d[, 1:p]))
y_s_list <- lapply(data_s, function(d) Surv(d$time, d$status))

screen <- detect_transferable(
  X_t = X_target, y_t = y_target,
  X_s_list = X_s_list, y_s_list = y_s_list,
  rule = "median", min_prop_positive = 0,
  alpha = alpha, V = 5, seed = 123
)
summary(screen)
```

## 5. Estimate density-ratio weights

We use the calibration subset from the deployment population as the reference
distribution. `calculate_weights()` estimates an exponential-tilting
model between the denominator dataset (the data to be reweighted) and the 
numerator dataset (the deployment calibration data), then truncates and normalises 
the resulting weights. The truncation interval is set by `clip`, either as the two 
truncation probabilities or as a single central coverage: the default `clip = c(0.025, 0.975)` 
clips at the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, `clip = 0.95` is shorthand for the same interval.

```{r weights}
# External-to-deployment weights
w_source <- do.call(c, lapply(1:3, function(i) {
  calculate_weights(
    X_denominator = as.matrix(data_s[[i]][, 1:p]),
    X_numerator = X_calibrate,
    cv_lambda = FALSE,
    ncore = 1
  )$w
}))

# Target-to-deployment weights
weight_target <- calculate_weights(
  X_denominator = X_target,
  X_numerator = X_calibrate,
  cv_lambda = FALSE,
  ncore = 1
)
summary(weight_target)
w_target <- weight_target$w
```

## 6. Fit survival models

Each model is fitted with a single `fit_coxrtl()` call (the underlying
penalized-Cox and two-step transfer-learning routines are internal to the
package). Two survival modelling strategies, selected by the logical argument
`transfer`:

-   **`transfer = FALSE`**: penalized Cox model trained using only the target
    dataset;
-   **`transfer = TRUE`**: two-step transfer-learning model that borrows
    information from external datasets.

Either model can be fitted without weights, in which case it is not calibrated
for covariate shift, or with the density-ratio weights, in which case it is
recalibrated toward the deployment population. The target-only model consumes
the target weights `w_t` alone; the transfer model consumes `w_t` and the
external weights `w_s`. Both forms of both models are fitted below.

Requesting coefficient-level confidence intervals through `bootstrap = TRUE`
makes `fit_coxrtl()` return `list(beta, ci)` instead of a bare coefficient
vector. Under the hood `nboot` nonparametric resamples of the subjects are
drawn and the model is refitted at the full-data `lambda` on each resample. The
resampling is seeded via the `seed` argument, and when `ncore > 1` the
parallelisation acts across resamples rather than inside the cross-validation:

### Target-only model: `transfer = FALSE`

The target-only model uses the target dataset only, so `X_s` and `y_s` are not
supplied at all.

```{r nontransfer-unw, eval=FALSE}
nontransfer_unw <- fit_coxrtl(
  X_t = X_target, y_t = y_target,
  transfer = FALSE, alpha = alpha, lambda = lambda,
  type.measure = "deviance", seed = 123,
  bootstrap = TRUE, nboot = 100
)
```

### Target-only model, reweighted: `transfer = FALSE` with `w_t`

```{r nontransfer-w, eval=FALSE}
nontransfer_w <- fit_coxrtl(
  X_t = X_target, y_t = y_target,
  w_t = w_target,
  transfer = FALSE, alpha = alpha, lambda = lambda,
  type.measure = "deviance", seed = 123,
  bootstrap = TRUE, nboot = 100
)
```

### Transfer model: `transfer = TRUE`

```{r transfer-unw, eval=FALSE}
transfer_unw <- fit_coxrtl(
  X_t = X_target, X_s = X_s_all, y_t = y_target, y_s = y_s_all,
  transfer = TRUE, alpha1 = alpha, alpha2 = alpha, lambda = lambda,
  type.measure = "deviance", seed = 123,
  bootstrap = TRUE, nboot = 100
)
```

### Transfer model, reweighted: `transfer = TRUE` with `w_t` and `w_s`

```{r transfer-w}
transfer_w <- fit_coxrtl(
  X_t = X_target, X_s = X_s_all, y_t = y_target, y_s = y_s_all,
  w_t = w_target, w_s = w_source,
  transfer = TRUE, alpha1 = alpha, alpha2 = alpha, lambda = lambda,
  type.measure = "deviance", seed = 123,
  bootstrap = TRUE, nboot = 100
)
summary(transfer_w, head = 10)         # top coefficients with interval bounds
head(as.data.frame(transfer_w$ci))     # se / lower / upper for the
```

## 7. Evaluate predictive performance

All models are evaluated on the held-out evaluation subset from the deployment
population.

```{r predict}
preds <- predict_coxrtl(X = X_evaldata, transfer_w)$pred
risks <- predict_coxrtl(X = X_evaldata, transfer_w)$risk
```

### 7.1 Harrell's C-index

```{r cindex}
cindex <- survcomp::concordance.index(
    x = preds,
    surv.time = data_evaldata$time,
    surv.event = data_evaldata$status,
    method = "noether"
  )$c.index
cindex
```

### 7.2 Time-dependent AUC

Because each `timeROC` object stores one AUC per time point, we summarise the
models at three representative time points (the 25%, 50% and 75% quantiles of
the event times in the evaluation set):

```{r auc-readme}
eval_times <- as.numeric(quantile(data_evaldata$time[data_evaldata$status == 1], c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)))
auc <- timeROC(
    T = data_evaldata$time,
    delta = data_evaldata$status,
    marker = preds,
    cause = 1,
    weighting = "marginal",
    times = eval_times
  )
auc
```


### 7.3 Brier score

The Brier score is evaluated at 100 time points spanning the event times in
the evaluation set (as in the README), and reported as the integrated error
(`ierror`).

```{r test}
preds_train <- predict_coxrtl(X = X_target, transfer_w)$pred

# Evaluation time points
times <- c(0.77, 1.47, 2.20, 2.93)

# Calculate Brier scores
briers <- predErr <- survAUC::predErr(
    Surv.rsp = Surv(
      data_target$time,
      data_target$status
    ),
    Surv.rsp.new = Surv(
      data_evaldata$time,
      data_evaldata$status
    ),
    lp = as.matrix(preds_train),
    lpnew = as.matrix(preds),
    times = times,
    type = "brier",
    int.type = "weighted"
  )
predErr
```
